scope: Native Chromium lostpointercapture regression for the existing canvas-safe floating dock drag lifecycle.

test.name: losing floating dock pointer capture restores the last saved position without a stale pointerup commit
test.assertions: Uses a real Chromium mouse gesture and native pointer capture. It observes the assigned pointer id and transient drag, revokes capture using releasePointerCapture, waits for lostpointercapture cleanup, then sends a stale mouseup. The saved dock position and live CSS offsets return to (0,0), existing Undo/Redo state is unchanged, and Page Model/Save/Publish request and browser-error logs remain empty.
test.first_attempt: The test initially assumed Undo must be disabled after its own workspace setup. The setup intentionally creates history, so this was an invalid baseline expectation rather than a product failure. The regression now snapshots Undo/Redo state after setup and asserts cancellation leaves that state unchanged.
test.targeted_result: PASS 1/1 in Chromium; the test fixture subreaper reaped four orphan descendants.

viewport_resize_during_drag.name: resizing the viewport during a floating dock drag cancels transient movement and preserves the saved position
viewport_resize_during_drag.targeted_result: PASS 1/1 in Chromium; the browser fixture subreaper reaped four orphan descendants.
viewport_resize_during_drag.assertions: A native mouse drag moves the floating dock transiently from a saved mid-lane position. Resizing 1920px to 1025px cancels the drag; stale mouseup does not commit the transient position; the card stays in its reserved lane, the canvas remains at least 400 CSS px and is not overlapped, and returning to 1920px restores the exact persisted position with no active movement class.
viewport_resize_during_drag.initial_attempt: The first test attempt started from the End-key maximum, leaving no room for the subsequent pointer movement. This was a test setup error, not a runtime failure; the baseline now uses Home followed by one ArrowRight and ArrowDown step.
